pages.text: Early in the morning, people line up at the corn mill with bowls of soaked maize. The miller presses a button. With a rising hum, a heavy machine begins to spin and the grinding plates start to turn. Nobody is pushing them. No animal is pulling. Electricity flows in through a cable, and movement comes out. The machine that does this is an electric motor. There is one in every fan, fridge, blender, water pump, and sewing machine, and a tiny one makes your phone vibrate. How can electricity make something turn?

pages.alt: A corn mill in a small shed, with customers holding bowls of maize waiting in a line.

pages.text: The first clue came by accident in 1820. A Danish teacher, Hans Christian Oersted, was showing his students an electric circuit. A compass happened to be lying near the wire. Each time he switched the current on, the compass needle swung away from north. When he switched off, it swung back. A compass needle moves only when a magnet is near, so the wire must have been acting as a magnet. Oersted had shown that an electric current produces a magnetic field around it. Electricity and magnetism, which everyone had thought were separate, were connected.

pages.alt: A compass lying under a wire that is joined to a battery, with its needle turned away from north.

pages.text: You can use this at once. Wind insulated wire many times round an iron nail and join the ends to a battery. The nail picks up pins. Disconnect the battery and the pins fall. You have made an electromagnet: a magnet that can be switched on and off. More turns of wire or a larger current make it stronger. Scrap yards use giant electromagnets to lift old cars and drop them again. An electric bell uses a small one to pull its hammer. Every electric motor has electromagnets inside it.

pages.alt: An iron nail wound with wire and joined to a battery, with pins hanging from its tip.

pages.text: Now put a coil of wire between the poles of a magnet and pass a current through it. The coil becomes an electromagnet, and the fixed magnet pushes one side of it up and the other side down, so the coil turns. Just as it is about to stop, a clever sliding contact reverses the current. The push changes direction and the coil keeps turning, round and round. Fix the coil to a shaft and the shaft will spin a fan blade, a pump, or a grinding plate. A motor turns electrical energy into kinetic energy, the energy of movement.

pages.alt: A coil of wire on a shaft between the two poles of a magnet, with curved arrows showing it turning.

pages.text: Motors do far more than save effort. A motor-driven pump lifts clean water from a borehole. In hospitals, motors pump blood through dialysis machines for people whose kidneys have failed, and they drive the tools that surgeons control from a screen. Small motors inside modern artificial hands let a person who has lost a hand grip a cup or hold a pen. On the roads, electric motorcycles, tricycles, and cars are beginning to appear in Ghana’s cities. They are quiet, and they give out no exhaust smoke, because a motor burns no fuel.

pages.text: A motor and a generator are the same machine run in opposite directions. Feed in electricity and you get movement: a motor. Turn the shaft by force and you get electricity: a generator. No motor is perfect. Some of the electrical energy is always wasted as heat and sound, which is why a motor feels warm after use. Look after motors and they last. Keep them clean and dry, do not overload them, and switch off when the work is done. Next time the mill begins to hum, you will know that a current and a magnet are doing the work.

activities.question: What did Oersted’s experiment show?
options: An electric current produces a magnetic field

activities.question: How can you make an electromagnet stronger?
options: Use more turns of wire or a larger current

activities.question: What energy change takes place in an electric motor?
Apply it: After grinding for an hour, the casing of a mill motor feels warm. What is the best explanation?
options: Some of the electrical energy is wasted as heat
The motor has stopped using electricity

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order to explain how a motor turns.
items: A current is passed through the coil
The fixed magnet pushes the two sides of the coil in opposite directions
The current is reversed so the coil keeps turning

activities.definition: A magnet made by passing a current through a coil of wire; it can be switched on and off.
distractors: A magnet that never loses its strength
A battery with a magnet inside it

glossary.definition: A machine that turns electrical energy into movement.
Magnetic field: the region around a magnet where its force can be felt.
A magnet made by passing a current through a coil of wire.
Kinetic energy: the energy of movement.
A machine that produces electricity when its shaft is turned.
